transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-04
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Aurelia Head of ML), Greta Linde (Aurelia Platform Lead), Jordan Morris (Aurelia Product Ops)

Summary:
Quick run-through of Aurelia's rollout timeline and cost targets, confirm Dedicated pilot vs hosted staging, security clearance items, and owners for the perf benchmark. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pilot SOW + pricing, security packet; SE to run performance design; Aurelia to supply prompt set and usage profile.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and pass/fail criteria
- Cost per token vs latency tradeoffs (batching, quantization)
- Private/Dedicated network options (VPC/VPN, on-prem considerations)
- Security: SOC2/ISO, KMS/HSM, audit logs, data residency
- Rollout plan: canary, A/B, automatic fallback and rollback owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. we wanted to make sure we align on the pilot scope and who owns which bits for the rollout. how's every— how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Samir Patel: Good, thanks. we had a couple internal blockers last week but looks like we can move forward, asking mainly about latency targets and cost for peak traffic.
[00:22] Diego Rivera: Cool. so from the SE side we'll design the benchmark harness to target both p50/p95 latency and token cost under your expected traffic. one question, Samir: are you leaning dedicated capacity or hosted for the pilot?
[00:38] Samir Patel: leaning dedicated for predictability but are worried about the commit. we want a 90-day pilot with minimal upfront and an ability to scale after. also, data residency — some user data must stay in eu-west region.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Totally get it. we can do Dedicated with a short-term commitment for pilot; propose a reserved pool size that you can scale. we'll include burst policies in the SOW so you don't get throttled during tests.
[01:03] Greta Linde: On residency, we need the control plane in our VPC and keys managed by our KMS; are those supported?
[01:10] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations and an option for customer-managed VPC. for the pilot we'd recommend VPC peering or private endpoint.
[01:22] Jordan Morris: Quick clarification — if we pick Dedicated but keep control plane in Redwood, does Redwood have access to logs? we need auditability but also strict RBAC.
[01:33] Diego Rivera: Good question. audit logs are available and can be forwarded to your SIEM. RBAC can be scoped to token-level in the console. also note that logs can be configured to redact user PII.
[01:47] Samir Patel: ok, can you send an example retention and log schema so we can check with security?
[01:52] Maya Chen: yes, we'll attach the security packet with SOC 2 summary, ISO notes, and a sample log schema.
[02:00] Jordan Morris: great. about latency: We need p95 < 350ms for short prompts, but long multi-turn conversations sometimes spike. is that achievable?
[02:10] Diego Rivera: depends on model choice and batching. for low-latency we can route to a lower-quantized variant or smaller context model; tradeoff is slight quality hit. we also do KV cache warmup and continuous batching strategies to reduce hot-path latency.
[02:26] Samir Patel: so what's the expected token cost difference if we move to a quantized 4-bit model vs fp16?
[02:33] Diego Rivera: rough ballpark: quantized can be 30-60% cheaper at decode time, but training/quality delta exists. we'll include model/quantization recommendations in the perf write-up with measured token/sec and latency.
[02:46] Priya Nair: one thing we saw with other customers is cold-start penalties — Diego, can we add cold start to the benchmark?
[02:53] Diego Rivera: yes, we'll include cold-start scenarios and cache priming tests.
[03:00] Samir Patel: timeline — we want to go live with an internal canary in Jan, then external beta in Feb. is that workable?
[03:08] Maya Chen: yes, it's tight but doable if we lock requirements this week and get the SOW signed. pilot SOW will be 90 days; canary owners and rollback playbook must be in place.
[03:18] Greta Linde: We also need confirmation around model rollouts — ability to do canary with automatic fallback to older model if latency/quality regresses. that's non-negotiable for product.
[03:29] Diego Rivera: Redwood supports per-route rollouts: canary %, A/B, and automatic fallback policies based on error/latency thresholds. we'll show the console flows in the demo.
[03:41] Jordan Morris: Another ask — cost visibility per route and per token for shared models, granular enough for product owners.
[03:48] Priya Nair: the Console has token-level and route-level breakdowns; we can share a sample dashboard export.
[03:55] Samir Patel: Great. On procurement — legal will want a SOC2 report and a data processing addendum. will you provide those during the pilot?
[04:04] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include the SOC 2 Type II artifact and a standard DPA. for additional controls we can add in the pilot amendment.
[04:12] Greta Linde: Security will likely ask about key provenance — customer KMS or HSM?
[04:18] Diego Rivera: We support customer-managed KMS; HSM integrations are available for Private deployments. we'll note supported providers in the packet.
[04:27] Samir Patel: ok. cost modeling aside — we need a predictable number for budgeting. can you give a sample three-scenario estimate: conservative, expected, high?
[04:36] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll include 3 scenarios tied to token volumes (100k, 500k, 1M token/mo) and show cost per-token projections with and without batching/quantization savings.
[04:49] Jordan Morris: For the pilot success criteria let's put measurable goals: p95 latency <350ms, token cost <$0.0009 per token for expected workload, model accuracy delta <2% vs baseline.
[05:02] Maya Chen: agreed. I'll capture those as the pilot pass/fail criteria.
[05:07] Samir Patel: One more thing — we need a runbook for degraded states and automatic fallback. who's the owner on Redwood for rollbacks?
[05:16] Diego Rivera: SE will own the rollback playbook; Priya will own communication and escalation. we'll include contacts in the SOW.
[05:24] Priya Nair: yes, I'll be point for on-call coordination and escalation doc.
[05:29] Maya Chen: Recap of action items: I'll send SOW + pricing and security packet. Diego will prepare the benchmark plan. Samir will send the prompt set and volume projection. Priya will schedule the stakeholder meeting.
[05:45] Samir Patel: Sounds good. one note — we might have to add the legal procurement timeline to the SOW; we usually take 3-4 weeks to sign.
[05:52] Maya Chen: we will call that out. ok, thanks everyone.

End recap (final 3 minutes):
[53:00] Maya Chen: Next steps recap: 1) Redwood sends Dedicated pilot SOW and pricing (Maya) by 2026-12-09. 2) Security packet with SOC2 and KMS guides (Maya) by 2026-12-06. 3) Performance benchmark plan (Diego) by 2026-12-11. 4) Aurelia provides sample prompt set + usage projection (Samir) by 2026-12-08. 5) Priya to schedule internal kickoff with Aurelia security + legal by 2026-12-07.
[53:45] Jordan Morris: thanks, appreciate it.
[53:50] Greta Linde: thanks all.
[53:52] Maya Chen: We'll follow up with calendar invites and attach docs. bye.

Notes: Transcript includes occasional mis-transcriptions and shorthand common to meeting exports (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes rendered as 'cv cache' in automated text).
